result.description:
Community Worker

Business: V & C Nursing Pty Ltd
Location: Jordan Springs NSW 2747
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing
Salary: AUD $75,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation

Full Job Description

About the Business

V & C Nursing Pty Ltd is an Australian healthcare and community services provider located at 116 Lakeside Parade, Jordan Springs NSW 2747. The organisation delivers professional nursing, disability support, aged care, and community care services tailored to the needs of individuals requiring healthcare assistance and personalised support across New South Wales. V & C Nursing Pty Ltd provides a broad range of services, including disability support, community participation programs, personal care assistance, supported independent living (SIL), aged care services, transport assistance, household support, medication assistance, and individualised care programs designed to promote independence, wellbeing, and social inclusion.
Operating within Australia's highly regulated healthcare and community services sector, V & C Nursing Pty Ltd is committed to delivering high-quality, person-centred services that empower individuals living with disabilities, older Australians, and vulnerable members of the community to achieve meaningful and independent lives. The organisation works collaboratively with clients, families, healthcare professionals, allied health practitioners, support coordinators, and community organisations to deliver tailored support services aligned with individual goals and care requirements while maintaining compliance with relevant Australian healthcare and workplace legislation.
With increasing client demand, workforce growth, and expanding community support programs, V & C Nursing Pty Ltd requires an experienced Community Worker to coordinate participant supports, facilitate community engagement initiatives, promote client independence, and ensure the continued delivery of high-quality, person-centred services that contribute positively to client wellbeing and community participation.
 
About the Role

The Community Worker is responsible for assessing client needs, developing and implementing individual support strategies, coordinating access to healthcare and community resources, monitoring client progress, and assisting individuals to maximise their independence, wellbeing, and participation within the community.
Working closely with clients, families, healthcare professionals, support coordinators, allied health providers, carers, and external agencies, the Community Worker plays an integral role in delivering holistic and person-centred support services that promote social inclusion, personal development, and positive client outcomes consistent with V & C Nursing Pty Ltd's service delivery model.
The position requires excellent communication, interpersonal, organisational, and problem-solving abilities together with a genuine commitment to improving the quality of life of individuals receiving healthcare, disability, and community support services.
 
Key Responsibilities

•	Conduct client interviews and comprehensive needs assessments to identify individual goals, strengths, risks, and support requirements.
•	Develop, implement, monitor, and regularly review individual support plans consistent with client needs and service objectives.
•	Support clients to develop independent living skills, social skills, confidence, and meaningful community participation.
•	Assist clients in accessing healthcare services, allied health supports, aged care services, housing assistance, education, employment programs, transport services, and community resources.
•	Facilitate client participation in community activities, recreational programs, life skills initiatives, and social inclusion programs.
•	Monitor client wellbeing, evaluate service outcomes, maintain accurate case notes, and prepare progress reports as required.
•	Provide advocacy, information, guidance, and practical assistance to clients and their families regarding available healthcare and community support services.
•	Liaise with healthcare professionals, support coordinators, allied health practitioners, carers, government agencies, and community organisations to coordinate integrated and client-focused service delivery.
•	Identify barriers affecting client independence and implement appropriate support strategies that promote positive outcomes and enhanced quality of life.
•	Maintain confidential client records, incident reports, service documentation, and case management records in accordance with organisational policies and legislative requirements.
•	Promote client rights, dignity, privacy, cultural inclusion, and person-centred practice at all times.
•	Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, quality improvement initiatives, and ongoing professional development activities.
•	Assist V & C Nursing Pty Ltd in maintaining compliance with workplace health and safety legislation, relevant healthcare standards, and organisational policies and procedures.
•	Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance client satisfaction, service quality, and organisational performance.
 
Requirements

•	Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
•	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Community Services, Disability, Human Services, Individual Support, Welfare, Social Work, or a closely related field, or at least three years of relevant experience may substitute for formal qualifications where applicable (ANZSCO Skill Level 2).
•	Demonstrated experience working within disability services, community services, aged care, healthcare support services, or related environments.
•	Strong understanding of person-centred practice, client rights, safeguarding principles, and community service delivery models.
•	Sound knowledge of disability support services, aged care services, community resources, and client-centred care practices.
•	Excellent communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.
•	Strong organisational, case coordination, and problem-solving abilities.
•	Ability to maintain accurate client records and prepare professional reports.
•	Compassionate, empathetic, reliable, and client-focused approach to service delivery.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
•	Current National Police Check, Working with Children Check (where applicable), Current First Aid and CPR certification, or willingness to obtain.
•	Current Australian Driver Licence is desirable.
 
Work Conditions

•	Full-time, ongoing position.
•	Standard operational hours with flexibility based on client needs and service delivery requirements.
•	Work is performed across client homes, community settings, healthcare facilities, and outreach locations throughout New South Wales.
•	Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
•	Collaborative and supportive multidisciplinary environment committed to delivering high-quality healthcare and community support services.
•	Opportunity to contribute meaningfully to positive community outcomes by empowering individuals to achieve greater independence, wellbeing, and social inclusion through professional and compassionate support services.
result.title: Community Worker

About Us 

Amity Care Services is a Mornington Peninsula based disability and home care support provider, founded by a team of registered nurses with extensive clinical experience in complex and acute care. We deliver Supported Independent Living, Specialist Disability Accommodation, Short Term Accommodation, Support Coordination, Psychosocial Recovery Coaching and clinical nursing services across the region, and can provide 24/7 support to our clients. Our values of loyalty, trust and honesty shape how we work with each other and the people we support. 

About the Role 

We're looking for an experienced Rostering Lead to guide our Rostering team in delivering accurate, timely and person-centred rosters for our participants. Reporting to the Business Development Manager, you'll lead a team of rostering coordinators, ensuring the smooth day-to-day allocation of shifts while balancing compliance, staff wellbeing and participant needs in a fast-paced environment. 

This is a hands-on leadership role suited to someone who thrives on solving problems quickly, supporting a team under pressure, and keeping systems and communication running smoothly across departments. 

Key Responsibilities 

Lead and support a team of rostering coordinators in their day-to-day functions 

Ensure the smooth, consistent and compliant delivery of staff and participant rostering 

Oversee new participant and staff handovers, first shifts, and meet & greets 

Monitor staff compliance and skills, and manage overtime and field hours 

Maintain compliance with the SCHADS Award and NDIS pricing requirements 

Build strong working relationships across Recruitment, Clinical and Accounts 

Chair rostering meetings and represent the department at HOD meetings 

Conduct regular support and supervision with the rostering team 

About You 

At least 2 years' leadership or management experience 

At least 3 years' experience in rostering or scheduling, ideally within NDIS or Home Care Package frameworks 

Proven ability to lead a team, manage competing priorities and stay calm under pressure 

Excellent interpersonal, organisational and problem-solving skills 

Proficient in Microsoft Office and VisualCare (or similar rostering/care management platforms) 

A genuine interest in supporting vulnerable people in our community 

High-level written and verbal communication skills 

Requirements 

NDIS Worker Screening Check and Working with Children Check 

Completed NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission Orientation Module (or willingness to complete) 

Why Join Amity? 

Be part of a values-driven, growing organisation making a genuine difference 

Supportive leadership team and a collaborative, close-knit culture 

Opportunity to shape and lead a busy, high-impact department 

How to Apply 

To apply, please submit a written Expression of Interest (1–2 pages) addressing your motivation for the role, your understanding of the Rostering Lead position, and your leadership or mentoring experience, along with your current resume to recruitment@amitycareservices.com.au.

Assistant Accountant 
Company: ITV Studios Australia
Location: Sydney, NSW
Position Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Salary Range: $80,000 to $90,000 Plus Superannuation 

About Us
At ITV Studios Australia, we sit at the heart of global television, creating and delivering some of the country's most exciting, talked-about, and high-quality entertainment. 

The Role
Reporting to the Senior Financial Accountant, you will enjoy a highly varied 360-degree assistant accountant role. You will take true ownership of core transactional processes, keep our cash flow moving, and play a vital role in month-end and compliance reporting. You will be heavily involved in maintaining statutory compliance, and advising on internal accounting workflows.

Key Responsibilities & Tasks
Financial & Statutory Reporting:  Assist with preparation of the  financial statements for presentation to management, governing and statutory bodies.
Managing the general ledger including preparation and review of balance sheet reconciliations, banking and management of intercompany transactions and balances
Accounts Payable (AP): Take full ownership of the AP process, reconcile supplier statements, manage approvals within delegated authority limits, and maintain up-to-date supplier records.
Accounts Receivable (AR): Create and maintain debtor master files, raise milestone invoices for productions and ad-hoc invoices, maintain the AR database, and confidently follow up on outstanding balances.
Credit Cards & Banking Daily Operations: Administer our expense management system, manage staff credit cards (including adjusting limits), and import monthly submissions with precise GL coding and GST accuracy. Handle daily cash balance updates and weekly production account transfers.
Production Recharges: Own the end-to-end recharge process to Productions, including raising invoices for credit cards and AP recharges, preparing backup documentation, and following up.
Month-End Duties: Reconcile Head Office and production bank accounts, handle AP/AR trial balances, post month-end accruals, manage the Fixed Asset register (depreciation & GL reconciliation), and complete intercompany reconciliations.
Compliance Support: Assist with GST, WHT, and BAS returns, look after Payment Times Reporting, help set up new users/accounts on banking platforms, and support the wider finance team during the end-of-year audit.
About You
To be successful in this role, you should have a solid foundation in transactional accounting and a deep understanding of standard accounting procedures.

We are looking for:
At least 12 months relevant work experience in a varied Assistant Accountant role (experience in media, television, or entertainment is a huge plus!).
Strong technical understanding of AP, AR, bank reconciliations, and general ledger coding.
Solid grasp of Australian tax compliance, including GST, BAS, and withholding tax.
High attention to detail and intermediate-to-advanced Excel skills (you'll be working closely with spreadsheets and Google Sheets).
Excellent communication skills—you’ll be collaborating with production crew, external vendors, and internal stakeholders regularly.
A proactive mindset with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment.
Minimum Bachelor Degree or higher-level qualification in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline to satisfy the requirements of a professional Accountant role.

What’s on Offer?
The chance to work with a world-class, passionate, and fun media team.
A diverse role where no two days are the same—gaining exposure to corporate finance and production accounting.
Great office culture with opportunities for professional growth.

To Apply
If you are ready to take the next step in your accounting career with one of Australia's leading production companies, please click "Apply Now" and submit your resume along with a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience.

result.description: Ibavale Pty Ltd t/as Electronic Diesel Technology  Ibavale Pty Ltd, trading as Electronic Diesel Technology, is a family-owned Australian business that has proudly served the diesel industry for decades. We specialise in the repair, servicing and calibration of electronic injectors and common rail fuel injection systems for a range of diesel engine applications. We also supply truck engine parts, diagnostic tools, software, electrical connectors and related accessories for diesel engine platforms including Cat, Cummins, Detroit and Mack.  Due to continued business growth, we are seeking an experienced Senior Diesel Motor Mechanic / Diesel Fuel Injection Specialist to join our team.   Position Title:  Senior Diesel Motor Mechanic / Diesel Fuel Injection Specialist   Employment Type:  full time   Location:  WARRENHEIP VIC 3352   Benefits   Competitive remuneration package based on experience and technical capability.  Stable, long-term career opportunity with a well-established family-owned business.  Work on advanced diesel fuel injection systems and cutting-edge diagnostic technologies.  Opportunities for professional development and technical leadership.  Supportive team environment with a strong focus on quality and innovation.    Task & responsibilities   Serve as a senior technical lead for Diesel Injection Fuel Systems specifically for Heavy Duty and Large Engine applications, providing expert knowledge on diagnostics, repair and servicing of injectors, fuel pumps and related components.  Provide deep-dive troubleshooting, diagnostics, repair, testing, calibration, and oversight for Common Rail and Modular Common Rail Systems (MCRS) in accordance with manufacturer specifications and industry standards.   Review and refine existing diagnostic and repair procedures. Identify technical bottlenecks, and optimise workshop efficiency by applying technical expertise. Contribute to operational strategies and continuous improvement initiatives that support service capability expansion and business growth.   Develop and maintain comprehensive technical documentation, testing procedures and standardized operating procedures (SOPs) that facilitate company scaling and consistent service delivery.  Manage and mentor technical staff, fostering a culture of accountability. Maintain quality output and ensure all deliverables meet rigorous industry standards.  Monitor developments in diesel fuel injection systems and lead initiatives to implement improved diagnostic methods, testing procedures and repair techniques, as well as new product offerings and component solutions for newer generations of engines and advanced fuel systems.    Qualification & experience  We are seeking a results-driven professional with more than 10 years of experience and deep technical roots in Diesel Injection Fuel Systems to lead our technical operations. Certificate III in Automotive Diesel Engine Technology or equivalent is preferred. The ideal candidate will bridge the gap between complex technical and scalable workshop operations. You will be responsible for leading and overseeing the lifecycle of Common Rail and MCRS technologies while simplifying workflows to drive efficiency and team performance.   Essential skills for this role:    Mastery of Diesel Injection Systems for Heavy Duty/Large Engines.  Expert-level understanding of Common Rail and MCRS architecture.  Proven ability to perform complex diagnostics, testing, repair and calibration of diesel fuel injection components in accordance with manufacturer specifications.  Demonstrated skills to research, test, and implement advanced systems and repair techniques and products for newer engine technologies.  Proven ability to design, document, and implement highly efficient workflows.   If you have the skills, experience and passion to excel in this specialist role, we would love to hear from you.   Job Publish:  01-07-2026   Job Expire:  31-07-2026   Apply Link:  https://workinitiatives.com.au/job/details?id=5960284   This job is brought to you by workinitiatives.com.au.

result.description:
Farnese Australia Pty Ltd. is seeking a full Time Service Technician to join our team based in Ingleburn NSW.

Reporting to the Services Manager, this is a hands-on, permanent role where you will play a key part in machine installations, preventive and breakdown maintenance. You will work across mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic systems, servicing machinery such as CNC Machine Centres, Bridge Saws, Block Saws, and Jib / Gantry Cranes.
This role offers variety and the opportunity to work both autonomously and within a team. While qualifications are not essential, any mechanical or electrical aptitude will be highly regarded.

Key Responsibilities:
•	Perform preventive and breakdown maintenance of machinery.
•	Install, modify, maintain and repair complex and highly sophisticated electronic instruments and control systems which involve a combination of electrical, electronic and hydraulic and pneumatic principals.
•	Install and service equipment, including mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic components.
•	Interpret electrical drawings and perform diagnostic checks.
•	Liaise with clients to understand and address service requirements.

What We Offer:
•	A permanent, full-time role in a supportive team environment.
•	A company vehicle for both work and personal use.
•	Opportunity for hands-on, technical work with diverse, cutting edge equipment.

Essential Criteria
•	Ability to interpret electrical and mechanical concepts and drawings.
•	Ability to install, modify, maintain and repair complex and highly sophisticated electronic instruments and control systems which involve a combination of electrical, electronic and hydraulic and pneumatic principals.
•	Previous experience in machinery preventive maintenance.
•	Strong mechanical aptitude and fault-finding skills.
•	Excellent communication and client liaison skills.
•	Reliable work ethic with attention to detail and accuracy.
•	Ability to work independently or as part of a team.
•	Current driver's licence.
•	Minimum of less than 1 year of machinery preventive maintenance experience required.
•	Ability to interpret basic electrical symbols and drawings required.

Desirable Criteria:
•	Electrical fault-finding experience.
•	Knowledge of electrical control systems.
•	Experience with CNC machine technology and operation.
•	Background in the stone industry, manufacturing, or machinery service.

Renumeration: $85,000 - $105,000 + Super for the right candidate.

If you are looking for a hands-on, technically challenging role with the potential to grow and expand your skill set, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now and become an integral part of our team at Farnese Australia.
